 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Gwalior
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Ashish Shroti
 On The 30th Of January, 2026
 Writ Petition No. 19122 of 2022
 Gyadeen Jatav
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Jai Prakash Kushwah - Advocate for the petitione
 Shri K.K. Prajapati - Ga for the respondents/State.
 Order
Petitioner by filing instant petition seeking following reliefs:-

"The petitioner therefore most humbly prays that this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to allow the petition and the respondents /authority may kindly be directed to provide the retrial benefits to the petitioner."
2.

Facts necessary for decision of this case are that petitioner was initially appointed as Home Guard Sainik on 1/11/1989 under respondent no. 3 and worked till 30/12/2021 when he stood retired from service on attaining the age of 60 years.
Thus, the petitioner has rendered about 32 years of service in the respondent/department.
3. When the petitioner retired from service, he demanded payment of his retiral dues by making an application on 30/12/2021 before respondent no. 3.
However, when no response was received, the present petition was filed.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:3953 2 WP-19122-2022 4.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that petitioner has rendered more than 30 years of service in the respondent/department and he is therefore, entitled to the retiral dues.
It is his submission that denial of payment of retiral dues to the petitioner without there being any reason, is arbitrary and illegal.
He therefore, prayed for issuance of suitable directions to respondents.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State on the other hand referred to the averments made in the return and submitted that during the currency of his service, petitioner was tried for offence punishable under Section 366, 376 and 342 of IPC in ST No. 97/1994.

On account of his involvement in criminal case,
he was discharged from service on 4/1/1995.
Petitioner was thereafter, taken back in service on 12/10/1999.
He thus, submits that since the petitioner remained discharged from duty for the aforesaid period, as per the Govt. instructions, the petitioner is not entitled for payment of any dues.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioner taking this Court through the rejoinder submitted that petitioner was falsely implicated in the aforesaid criminal case and he is already acquitted vide judgment dated 1/3/1996 passed by Sessions Judge, Datia.
He thus submits that denial of payment of retiral dues is illegal.

7. Considered the arguments ad perused the record.
8.
Petitioner has prayed for payment of retiral dues in the present writ petition.
However, he has not clarified about the nature of retiral dues he was entitled for as Home Guard Sainik.
The return filed by the State is also silent on this aspect.

However, the State has filed copy of letter dated 23/1/2022 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:3953 3 WP-19122-2022 addressed to the petitioner,
wherein reference of Sanchit Nidhi is made.
It is stated in the said letter that since petitioner was discharged during his service, he is not entitled for payment of Sanchit Nidi.
Thus, petitioner's entitlement for payment of Sanchit Nidhi alone is considered in this order.
9. The entitlement of a Home Guard Sainik to receive Sanchit Nidhi was considered by this Court in the case of Rambharosa Meena Vs. State of M.P. & Ors. in W.P.No. 9086/2023 .

entities.text: Rambharosa Meena Vs. State of M.P. & Ors. in W.P.No. 9086/2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The aforesaid benefit flows from the Finance Department order dated 6/2/2013, wherein, the Home Guard Sainik has been held entitled for certain amount on account of his having worked for 10 years or more.
This amount has been termed as Sanchit Nidhi.
Said order further provides that if an incumbent is discharged from service at any point of time during his entire service, he would not be entitled for payment of Sanchit Nidhi.
Presumably, under the said clause of order dated 6/2/2013, the benefit has been denied to the petitioner.
10. This Court in the case of Rambharosa Meena (supra) also took into account the subsequent order passed by the Finance Department on 15/12/2023.

The relevant extract of this order is reproduced hereunder:-
"

6.Learned Senior Counsel referred to an order, dated 15.12.2023, issued by Finance Department of the State Government and submitted that after issuance of this order,
the petitioner is entitled to the amount of Sanchit Nidhi for the period excluding the period in which he remained discharged from service.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents submitted that since the petitioner had already retired on 31.12.2021, the order, dated 15.12.2023, would not be applicable in the petitioner's case and the said order would apply prospectively.

Therefore, the issue for consideration is as to whether the provisions of order, dated 15.12.2023, are applicable to the petitioner's case not ?

substituted condition has to be read in the order, dated 06.02.2013, right from the inception and it cannot be said that the changed condition would be applicable prospectively w.e.f. 15.12.2023.

The view of this Court finds support from the law laid down by Apex Court in the case of Shamarao V. Parulekar Vs. The District Magistrate, Thana, Bombay & Ors. reported in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:3953 5 WP-19122-2022 (1952) 2 SCC 1 wherein the Apex Court held in para-7 as under;
"7.

entities.text: Shamarao V. Parulekar Vs. The District Magistrate, Thana, Bombay & Ors. reported in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:3953 5 WP-19122-2022 (1952) 2 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The construction of an Act which has been amended is now governed by technical rules and we mast first be clear regarding the proper canons of construction.

The rule is that when a subsequent Act amends an earlier one in such a way as to incorporate itself, or a part of itself, into the earlier, then the earlier Act must thereafter be read and construed (except where that would lead to a repugnancy, inconsistency or absurdity) as if the altered words had been written into the earlier Act with pen and ink and the old words scored out so that thereafter there is no need to refer to the amending Act at all.

This is the rule in England:see Craies on Statute Law, 5th edition, page 207; it is the law in America: see Crawford on Statutory Construction,
page 110; and it is the law which the Privy Council applied to India in Keshoram Poddar v. Nundo Lal Mallick.

entities.text: Keshoram Poddar v. Nundo Lal Mallick
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Bearing this in mind it will be seen that the 1950 Act remains the 1950 Act all the way through even with its subsequent amendments.

Therefore, the moment 1952 Act was passed and section 2 came into operation, the Act of 1950 meant the 1950 Act as amended by section 2, that is to say, 1950 Act now due to expire on the 1-10-1952."

Again in the case of Income Tax Officer Vs. Vikram Sujitkumar Bhatia reported in (2024) 7 SCC 741 , the Apex Court reiterated the similar legal position in para-54 as under;
"54.

entities.text: Income Tax Officer Vs. Vikram Sujitkumar Bhatia reported in (2024) 7 SCC 741
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As observed hereinabove, Section 153-C has been amended by way of substitution whereby the words "belongs or belong to" have been substituted by the words "pertains or pertain to".

As observed and held by this Court in the case of Shamrao V. Parulekar that amendment by substitution has the effect of wiping the earlier provision from the statute book and replacing it with the amended provision as if the unamended provision never existed."

11.In view of the aforesaid legal position, it is evident that an amendment by substitution has the effect of wiping the earlier provision from the statute book and replacing it with the amended provision as if the unamended provision never existed.
Thus, the provision of order, dated 15.12.2023, would apply w.e.f. 06.02.2013.
The petitioner is, therefore, entitled to the benefit of Sanchit Nidhi for the period excluding the period of his discharge from 15.02.991 to 31.05.1996."

11. In view of aforesaid, it is clear that the petitioner is entitled for NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:3953 6 WP-19122-2022 Sanchit Nidhi excluding the period of discharge from 4/1/1995 to 12/10/1999.
12. Accordingly, petition is partly allowed.
Respondent are directed to confer the benefit of Sanchit Nidhi to the petitioner after excluding the aforesaid period of discharge.
Let needful be done within 90 days from the date of production of certified copy of this order.
13. Petition stands partly allowed and disposed of accordingly.

(ASHISH SHROTI) JUDGE JPS/-
